Membership is what made me stay. I have saved a lot here, and I have gotten a lot done in one stop. More than paying $25 a month+taxes I ended saving a hundreds of dollars!!

Perks is the part I actually use. I get upto 20% off my bills and 20% off grooming. I also earn rewards when I buy Petco branded stuff: wipes, accessories, treats, food. That adds up if you are in here the way pet parents are in here.

Grooming is why I trust this location. Nick G., the store manager, and groomer Joan are the best of the lot. I leave feeling like my pet was handled by people who care, not by a rotation that forgot the name.

I enrolled my 2 year old Frenchie, Gigi, at Petco for the beginner training classes. We took the group class but it wound up only being two dogs in the group including Gigi. I think the price is very reasonable. I was assigned to the trainer Lilly and I am very pleased with my dog’s progress! Gigi is a good dog overall, but I didn’t work as hard as I could have when she was a puppy to train her, so I was anxious that maybe staring to train her when she was 2 years old may be too late. I was wrong, because Lilly had done a great job at teaching Gigi and I long term methods and keys to keeping your dog in check. Lilly is very kind and has a lot of patience when teaching. She is also very knowledgeable about dogs so if I ever came to her with a problem she always had a solution or would help me think of one.

After finishing the 6 weeks beginners course Gigi is definitely more obedient and listens more overall, which was one of the main things I wanted to take away from the class.

Gigi and I will take the advanced class with Lilly and i’m convinced that she will make great process there as well. We are looking forward to it, and certainly recommend requesting Lilly as a trainer.

I also take Gigi to Petco for their grooming services. I think they do a great job, and Gigi always looks and feels nice and clean. She also smells clean for a long time. Their prices are reasonable here as well!

My experience with Vetco was honestly 50/50. I would not recommend this service if you have high expectations for personalized or consistent care. In my opinion, it’s best suited for the affordable vaccination package deals, especially for first-time pet vaccinations and that’s really where the value is.

One thing to keep in mind is that almost every follow-up appointment may be handled by a different team of veterinary staff. Because of that, visits can sometimes feel a bit disorganized or like the staff isn’t fully familiar with your pet’s history. It’s important to remember that it’s not always the same team working each time, so try not to be too hard on them they’re doing their best within the structure of the service.

Would I personally use this service again? No. As mentioned, it served its purpose for the initial vaccination package, but if you’re seeking consistent, high-quality care and a more personalized experience, I would recommend visiting your local veterinarian or animal hospital instead.

Again, no need to be harsh toward the staff just understand what this service is really best for before booking.

Dear Petco Customer Service,

Thank you for your prompt reply. While I appreciate the speed of your response, I must emphasize that the explanation provided does not address the core issue.

This is not an isolated incident—it is a recurring pattern. Each time I place an order, items listed as available turn out to be out of stock only after checkout, and the only substitutions offered are consistently higher‑priced alternatives. I have never once been offered a lower‑priced or equal‑value replacement. This makes your claim of **feigned ignorance** at the practice difficult to believe.

The user interface compounds the problem by making it extremely difficult to determine what exactly is being substituted. Customers are left in the dark until after the order is processed, at which point the only options are to accept the more expensive item or cancel the entire order. This is not a meaningful choice—it is a pressure tactic.

While I understand that legally this may not meet the strict definition of bait‑and‑switch, it certainly skirts the line and erodes customer trust. The consistent pattern of unavailable lower‑priced items being replaced with higher‑priced ones suggests more than mere incompetence. It feels exploitative.

****At a time when prices are skyrocketing and many pet owners are struggling to afford basic care—some even forced to abandon their pets—these practices are especially harmful. ****. Petco presents itself as a company dedicated to supporting pets and their families, yet these actions undermine that mission.

I am requesting:
- A refund for the substituted items charged at higher prices.
- Fulfillment of the products I originally ordered, or equal‑value replacements.
- A clear explanation of how Petco intends to correct this ongoing issue so that customers can trust the accuracy of your listings.

Shame on Petco for allowing such practices to persist. I expect accountability and corrective action, not feigned ignorance.

Repeated issue with inaccurate inventory and forced “upgrades.”

I’ve run into the same problem with this Petco location multiple times when ordering through Uber Eats: items are listed as available, but as soon as the order is placed, I’m told the product is “out of stock” and the only substitutes offered are noticeably more expensive.

This isn’t a one‑off inventory mistake — it’s a recurring pattern. The lower‑priced item is always the one that suddenly becomes unavailable, and the suggested alternatives always cost more. When you’ve already added other items that depend on the original product, you’re put in a position where declining the substitution means cancelling the entire order and starting over somewhere else. That’s not a real choice; it’s pressure created by the system.

Whether intentional or not, this setup creates a situation where customers are consistently pushed toward higher‑priced items after checkout. If this is happening to you too, I encourage you to report it to Uber Eats and Petco corporate so they can address the pattern. Accurate inventory and transparent pricing are basic expectations, and customers shouldn’t have to pay more simply to avoid wasting time.

While I enjoy coming to this Petco I won’t be coming to this location anymore,

Observation: A high customer volume was present, resulting in a long queue. Only one employee was actively assisting customers while an additional employee remained idle and did not engage in customer service tasks.

The problem was the other employee, a woman who was just sitting on her phone, drinking Coca-Cola, laughing, and playing games like she was on a break. She looked like she was having a great time — while completely ignoring customers and doing absolutely nothing.

Because of her behavior, a huge line formed, and everyone had to wait unnecessarily while ONE employee handled everything alone. This is extremely unprofessional and disrespectful to customers — and unfair to the employee who was actually working.

If someone is scheduled to work, they should do their job, not sit on their phone and ignore customers while the store backs up with people waiting.
